title: The canonical discrete and completed scalar square of the Tate twist
statement:
For a scheme S, a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], let A=(Z_l)_S and B=(O_E)_S be constant commutative ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let R=lim_r (Z/l^(r+1))_S and T=lim_n (O_E/(pi^(n+1)))_S [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the literal quotient maps as tower transitions. The maps A→R and B→T are the unique limit lifts of the quotient cones. The map Z_l→O_E is the unique map agreeing with the coefficient field inclusion, and induces A→B. The map R→T is uniquely characterized after every finite projection by a finite Z/l^r factorization of Z_l→O_E/(pi^n). These maps form a commutative square. Its comparison is the canonical morphism from the pushout of A→R and A→B to T. All of these are the unchanged named constructions extracted from the parent module; no assertion of invertibility or local freeness is included.

proof.text: Retain the original constant sheaves, quotient maps and tower limits. Limit universal properties give existence and uniqueness of the constant-to-completion maps. Integrality supplies the unique coefficient-ring inclusion. Each coefficient quotient kills a power of l; its factorization through Z/l^r yields a compatible cone, hence the completed scalar map. Cancellation of the epimorphic constant quotient maps and joint faithfulness of limit projections prove uniqueness and commutativity of the scalar square. Define its comparison by pushout.desc. These are exactly the already proved parent constructions, moved to avoid an import cycle with the coefficient-only tensor lemma.
